explain.say: Fresh water freezes at 0 degrees Celsius, but typical seawater must cool to about minus 1.9 degrees. It also takes longer, because the cold surface water keeps sinking and mixing until the whole top layer is that cold.

faq.q: Why does seawater freeze at a lower temperature?
faq.a: Salt dissolved in the water gets in the way of water molecules locking together into ice. Typical seawater must cool to about minus 1.9 degrees Celsius before it freezes.
asks: What temperature does the sea freeze at?

faq.a: Round slabs of slushy ice, from a few centimetres to a few metres across, with raised rims from bumping into each other. They form when waves stir freezing grease ice, and later freeze together into solid ice.
Much less than seawater. Most of the salt is pushed out as brine when the ice freezes, and old sea ice becomes fresh enough that polar explorers melted it for drinking water.
asks: Can you drink melted sea ice?

faq.q: How thick does sea ice get?
faq.a: Ice that forms in one winter is usually up to about 2 metres thick. Ice that survives several years in the Arctic can be 3 to 4 metres thick or more.

faq.q: Does melting sea ice raise sea levels?
faq.a: Hardly at all, because floating ice already pushes aside its own weight of water. Melting ice on land, like glaciers and ice sheets, does raise sea levels.
asks: Why does melting land ice matter more?

facts: Seawater of normal saltiness freezes at about minus 1.9 degrees Celsius.
Arctic sea ice is usually smallest each September and largest each March.

quiz.say: When seawater freezes into sea ice, where does most of the salt go?
quiz.show: When the sea freezes, most of the salt…

options.show: Is squeezed out as brine that sinks

options.show: Stays trapped as salt crystals in the ice
options.say: Stays trapped as salt crystals in the ice

quiz.why: Growing ice crystals push most of the salt out, making cold, salty brine that sinks into the ocean below.

wrong.1: Only a little brine gets trapped in pockets, and it drains out over time.
wrong.2: Salt does not evaporate or turn into gas when water freezes.
